scope_basis: Complete review of the original brief, revealed plan, frozen investigator package, independent critique and critic source map. Source IDs and identities are carried unchanged; disputed claims were independently rechecked in governing primary publisher sources.

sources.title: ISO 5348:2021 — Mechanical mounting of accelerometers
sources.released_version_or_commit: ISO 5348:2021, Edition 3, published 2021-01; official page says confirmed 2026-07-16 and current.
sources.locator: Official ISO page, abstract and lifecycle lines 4–50, 83–97, 138–142.
sources.observed_operation: Describes properties and recommended practice for contacting vibration-transducer mounts; says mounting can affect frequency response and measurement fidelity.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Applies to contacting uniaxial/multiaxial accelerometers and velocity transducers; other influences (alignment, base bending, cable motion, temperature, fields, cable whip, torque) are listed but out of scope.
sources.applicability: Use to motivate mount characterization and account for orientation/fastening; does not state what mount the cart has or diagnose the bracket.

critic_independent_verification.access: Official ISO page opened; not relied on for substantive claims in this critique because its page carries a non-AI-use notice. Mounting claims were checked against S02/S03.
critic_independent_verification.locator_checked: Official page metadata/abstract was encountered; no substantive source text reproduced in critique.
critic_independent_verification.scope: Identity/version mapping preserved from investigator record; no cart-specific inference.

sources.title: TE Connectivity, Guidelines for Adhesive Mounting Accelerometers
sources.released_version_or_commit: ©2017 TE Connectivity; one-page application note; no revision number shown.
sources.locator: Page 1, opening paragraph and mounting guidelines.
sources.observed_operation: States stiffer coupling raises mounted natural frequency; magnetic is least stiff and stud/screw most stiff; recommends a thin adhesive layer when using cyanoacrylate.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Guidance is specific to adhesive mounting; temperature range for cited cyanoacrylate is −18 to 125 °C; surface should be flat, clean; the document disclaims application suitability warranties.
sources.applicability: Only an illustrative alternative if the cart uses an adhesive or removable mount; do not prescribe this adhesive for an unknown sensor/surface.

critic_independent_verification.access: Official TE PDF opened and read.
critic_independent_verification.locator_checked: Page 1: mounting stiffness and mounted natural frequency; clean/flat surface and thin adhesive-layer guidance.
critic_independent_verification.scope: Adhesive-specific vendor guidance; supports a conditional mechanism only, not an unknown cart mount.

sources.title: Endevco Technical Paper 312 — Guide to Adhesively Mounting Accelerometers
sources.released_version_or_commit: Technical Paper 312; vendor PDF URL dated 2019-02; no revision identifier observed.
sources.locator: Pages 1–5, purpose, mounting recommendations, tested-model examples and material-specific restrictions.
sources.observed_operation: Reports mount coupling stiffness affects natural frequency; describes tests of models 751-100 and 2226C and examples of adhesive/magnet limits.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Results are limited to the listed sensors, adhesives, test conditions, frequencies, temperatures and amplitudes; e.g. vendor cautions magnet mounts only at lower frequencies and hot glue above 93 °C.
sources.applicability: Supports treating mount method as a transfer-function variable; numerical frequency limits are not transferable to unknown cart hardware.

critic_independent_verification.access: Official Endevco PDF opened and read.
critic_independent_verification.locator_checked: Pages 1–5: coupling stiffness, tested models, adhesives, and method-specific limits.
critic_independent_verification.scope: Results depend on the cited sensor models and test conditions; no cart performance transfer.

sources.title: Railway Track Monitoring Using Train Measurements: An Experimental Case Study
sources.released_version_or_commit: Malekjafarian et al., Applied Sciences 2019, 9(22), 4859; DOI 10.3390/app9224859; published 2019-11-13.
sources.locator: Abstract and sections 1, 3–5 (60-pass study, speed influence/correction, comparison with Track Recording Vehicle).
sources.observed_operation: Uses an in-service Irish train with accelerometers/GPS over two months; analyzes 60 passes on Dublin–Belfast and compares scaled signal energy to Track Recording Vehicle data.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Data selection removed passes below a speed limit and corrected remaining energy by measured speed; it is specific to that line/train/algorithm/reference.
sources.applicability: Supports logging speed, repeated passes and an independent geometry reference; no result or threshold transfers to the maintenance cart.

critic_independent_verification.access: Official MDPI article surfaced through publisher search excerpts; direct open returned an internal error.
critic_independent_verification.locator_checked: Publisher excerpt supports 60 passes and speed influence/correction; full article details were not independently re-read in this stage.
critic_independent_verification.scope: A rail precedent for repeat passes/speed/reference only; no cart thresholds or responses transfer.

sources.title: Development of railway track condition monitoring from multi-train in-service vehicles
sources.released_version_or_commit: Balouchi, Bevan & Formston, Vehicle System Dynamics 59(9), 1397–1417; online 2020-04-22, issue publication 2021-09-01; DOI 10.1080/00423114.2020.1755045.
sources.locator: Publisher full text, trials on Network Rail infrastructure and conclusions (Run 36 repeat; speed/GNSS alignment; vertical/lateral limits).
sources.observed_operation: A cab-based demonstrator was aligned with Network Rail New Measurement Train geometry using time/GNSS and compared speed; Run 36 repeated a section and detected the same location.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Authors report low/changing speed reduced correlation without speed compensation; vehicle response and suspension limit inference; lateral correspondence weaker than vertical.
sources.applicability: Supports a controlled repeat-pass and synchronization design, while showing that rail-car calibration and known-fault correlation are not cart evidence.

critic_independent_verification.access: Taylor & Francis full-text result and excerpts reviewed; direct open returned an internal error.
critic_independent_verification.locator_checked: Official excerpts describe speed compensation and Figures 16–18 comparing normalized 1/8-mile statistics for Run 25/Run 36 against NMT data; vertical agreement is stronger than lateral.
critic_independent_verification.scope: The excerpt does not substantiate the draft's stronger claim that a repeated run detected the same discrete reported location; see C1.

reviser_independent_verification.locator_checked: Publisher full-text search result, sections on speed compensation and Network Rail trials, Figure 9 text, and comparison of Runs 25 and 36.
reviser_independent_verification.access_operation: Official Taylor & Francis full-text result returned the article passage; direct open returned an internal error.
reviser_independent_verification.observed_operation: The article says the repeated Run 36 over the same section captured the same known track fault as Run 25. It describes matching speed/data sections against NMT and a longitudinal location offset from different GNSS antenna positions. Its trial also reports stronger vertical than lateral agreement and speed effects.
reviser_independent_verification.governing_condition_default_exception: A particular in-cab demonstrator, Thameslink/NMT route, known track fault, train response and GNSS configuration; the article describes speed compensation needs and acknowledges location offset. These conditions are specific to the rail study.
reviser_independent_verification.applicability: Supports the narrow statement that this rail demonstrator reported repeated capture of the same fault and the use of time/GNSS/speed alignment. It does not supply cart performance, a transferable threshold, or diagnosis for this case.
reviser_independent_verification.disposition: Critique C1's claim that the primary study did not establish repeated capture is rejected; the final wording is tightened to the article's rail-specific result and limits.

sources.title: Development and Operation of Track Condition Monitoring System Using In-Service Train
sources.released_version_or_commit: Tsunashima et al., Applied Sciences 2023, 13(6), 3835; DOI 10.3390/app13063835; PDF article version linked as version=1691324931.
sources.locator: Sections 2–3 and 7; PDF pages 3–7 and 18–19, especially measurement history, same-train note, speed note, position caveat, and maintenance comparison.
sources.observed_operation: Regional railway onboard accelerometer/gyro/GNSS deployment operated Oct 2020–Aug 2022; near-zero data Jan–Jun 2022 due to vehicle inspection/software updates; used time-position correction and track-geometry data.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Analysis used the same train because readings change with train; selected sections did not correct speed because reported variation was small. Section 2.3 gives the inspection/software-update gap as Jan–Jun 2022, while Section 3.3 gives Jan 2021–Jun 2022; the paper is internally inconsistent on the gap start. GNSS map matching and operator curve reference points also had stated location caveats.
sources.applicability: Operational history and explicit limits inform audit items; system, rail thresholds, vehicle dynamics and location corrections do not transfer to this cart.

critic_independent_verification.access: Official MDPI article/PDF search results reviewed; direct open returned an internal error.
critic_independent_verification.locator_checked: Publisher excerpts confirm long-term deployment, no measurement between January and June 2022, GNSS position error and correction; the complete cited sections were not independently recovered.
critic_independent_verification.scope: Operational history only; cart transfer is bounded. Investigator's noted internal gap-date inconsistency remains a source-level caveat.

sources.title: Experimental Study of Wheel-to-Rail Interaction Using Acceleration Sensors for Continuous Rail Transport Comfort Evaluation
sources.released_version_or_commit: Mihăilescu et al., Sensors 2023; PMCID PMC10574946, PMID 37836894; accepted 2023-09-22, collection date 2023-10.
sources.locator: Sections 2.1–2.3, 3.1–3.3 and 4; sensor/DAQ specifications, stored table rows, and discussion of empty vs loaded trials.
sources.observed_operation: A six-sensor tank-wagon study compares axle and car-body positions, empty and loaded, on a test ring; the hardware table reports 19.2 kS/s, the example export advances by 0.02 s (50 Hz), while discussion says 50 ms (20 Hz).
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Empty run was 125 km/h and loaded run 110 km/h, so load and speed are confounded. The paper does not reconcile the stated amplifier rate, tabulated 0.02 s increments, and 50 ms/20 Hz discussion. Findings and cadence are specific to this wagon/setup.
sources.applicability: Shows why mounting position, load, speed and background vehicle response must be logged and separated; neither its sample rate nor values set cart requirements.

critic_independent_verification.access: Full PMC article opened and checked.
critic_independent_verification.locator_checked: Table 2 amplifier specification; software/export table at 0.02 s; later text says 50 ms/20 Hz; unloaded 125 km/h versus loaded 110 km/h.
critic_independent_verification.scope: The paper's setup is internally inconsistent about cadence, and load is confounded with speed; neither rate transfers to the cart.

sources.title: Method for predicting dynamic loads for a health monitoring system for subway tracks
sources.released_version_or_commit: Romero Navarrete et al., Frontiers in Mechanical Engineering, article 858424 (2022); DOI 10.3389/fmech.2022.858424.
sources.locator: Sections 'Force estimation' and 'Experimental procedure', field/rig method and limitations, lines 351–379 of publisher text.
sources.observed_operation: A 1:10 rail rig measured cart speed optically, MEMS acceleration, and track strain; a rail-gap trigger synchronized channels; impact tests identified system natural frequencies.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Specific scaled rail geometry/model and operating conditions; authors note validation of analytical models is limited to particular conditions; a fixed strain gauge only captures its local passage response.
sources.applicability: Provides a concrete synchronized independent-reference design pattern, not a ready-made method or transfer function for this cart.

critic_independent_verification.access: Full Frontiers article opened and checked.
critic_independent_verification.locator_checked: Experimental procedure: 1:10 rig, optical speed, acceleration, strain gauges and rail-gap trigger; results explain the fixed gauge's local coverage.
critic_independent_verification.scope: A synchronized-reference design pattern only; the scaled rig and fixed sensor do not provide a cart transfer function.

reviser_independent_verification.release: Jauregui-Correa et al., Frontiers in Mechanical Engineering, volume 8, article 858424, published 2022-09-14; DOI 10.3389/fmech.2022.858424.
reviser_independent_verification.locator_checked: Force estimation / Experimental procedure, publisher lines 366–376; Empirical mode decomposition results, lines 407–412.
reviser_independent_verification.access_operation: Frontiers publisher article opened and the experimental setup and fixed-gauge locality text were read.
reviser_independent_verification.observed_operation: A 1:10 rig used optical speed, MEMS acceleration and fixed track strain gauges, with rail-gap triggering for synchronization. The authors say strain was significant when the railcar passed a fixed gauge and that a gauge would not register a dynamic condition at a remote track location.
reviser_independent_verification.governing_condition_default_exception: A scaled rail rig, fixed gauge positions and the authors' measurement arrangement; local coverage is explicit, but the arrangement is not the maintenance cart.
reviser_independent_verification.applicability: Supports synchronized reference design as an analogy and confirms that a null at one fixed location cannot exclude an event elsewhere. It does not establish cart diagnosis or whole-route coverage.
reviser_independent_verification.disposition: Critique C2 is accepted; a null-reference branch and reference-quality checks are added.

sources.title: STMicroelectronics LSM6DSM datasheet
sources.released_version_or_commit: DocID028165 Rev 7, dated September 2017; revision history at page 125 records Rev 6 (2017-05-03) and Rev 7 (2017-09-29).
sources.locator: Section 10.5 FIFO_CTRL2, Table 31; page 1 release metadata; revision history page 125.
sources.observed_operation: Describes a configurable digital 3-axis accelerometer/gyro, FIFO, ranges and register behavior; timestamp/step-counter FIFO data set is disabled by default.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Applies only to LSM6DSM. TIMER_PEDO_FIFO_EN default is 0; timestamp storage requires enabling it; defaults/configuration are not generic logger behavior.
sources.applicability: Example of why exact sensor ID and register configuration matter before relying on sample timestamps; no evidence this device is in the cart logger.

critic_independent_verification.access: Official ST datasheet PDF opened and checked.
critic_independent_verification.locator_checked: DocID028165 Rev 7, FIFO_CTRL2 and FIFO_CTRL4: timestamp/step dataset disabled by default; fourth-set decimation default is zero.
critic_independent_verification.scope: Applies only to LSM6DSM and its register configuration; no evidence that the cart uses it.

sources.title: ST AN4987 — LSM6DSM: always-on 3D accelerometer and 3D gyroscope
sources.locator: Section 3.7, pp.12–14 for accelerometer filtering chain/ODR bandwidth; p.114 Table 93 for revision history.
sources.observed_operation: Documents a multi-stage sampling/filter chain and configuration-dependent bandwidth, anti-alias and filter settling.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Anti-alias filter is enabled only in High-Performance mode; bandwidth depends on selected ODR and bits; applies to this exact sensor/configuration.
sources.applicability: Supports auditing actual filter and sampling settings; do not infer any cart logger behavior from this sample device.

critic_independent_verification.access: Official ST AN4987 Rev 5 PDF opened and checked.
critic_independent_verification.locator_checked: Section 3.7, pp. 12–14: analog anti-alias filter only in High-Performance mode, ODR-dependent bandwidth and filtering chain.
critic_independent_verification.scope: Configuration-specific example; no cart logger behavior inferred.

sources.title: ST technical support thread: LSM6DSM timestamp in FIFO occasionally incorrect
sources.released_version_or_commit: ST Community accepted answer by ST Technical Moderator, dated 2026-07-06; no device firmware/revision or formal erratum identified in the thread.
sources.locator: Accepted answer lines 62–80 and repeated answer lines 89–107.
sources.observed_operation: For one reported jumping/backward timestamp case, moderator says FIFO timestamp dataset/configuration and parsing may be responsible; recommends enabling dataset, checking pattern/order, and resetting counter after resolution change.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Scoped to LSM6DSM FIFO and the user's reported FIFO_CTRL4=0x08 setup; response says cause is likely/may explain, not a confirmed silicon defect.
sources.applicability: Illustrates version/config-specific support history to check if device matches; not evidence of a cart logger issue or proof of defect.

critic_independent_verification.access: ST Community thread opened and checked.
critic_independent_verification.locator_checked: Accepted moderator answer: timestamp issue is described as likely related to FIFO setup; timestamp dataset and FIFO decimation are both required.
critic_independent_verification.scope: Single configuration-specific support response, not a confirmed silicon defect or cart issue.

sources.title: Research on vibration fatigue of sensor bracket in a metro bogie based on the pseudo excitation method
sources.released_version_or_commit: Liu et al., Engineering Failure Analysis 145 (March 2023), Article 107046; DOI 10.1016/j.engfailanal.2022.107046.
sources.locator: Publisher abstract and sections 'Failure mode of sensor bracket in a metro car' and 'Field test'; article PII S1350630722010135.
sources.observed_operation: A field-tested metro bracket was modeled; paper reports a bracket mode near 61 Hz excited by rail corrugation impact as a fatigue contributor.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Specific 3.5-kg position sensor, C-shaped cantilever bracket, bolted metro bogie, operating line and validated model.
sources.applicability: Supports considering bracket resonance/flex as a possible mechanism after the reported bracket change; it cannot establish cart bracket behavior or failure.

critic_independent_verification.access: Elsevier ScienceDirect publisher search excerpt reviewed; direct open returned an internal error.
critic_independent_verification.locator_checked: Publisher abstract identifies a specific C-shaped bolted metro bracket and a modal vibration near 61 Hz associated with rail-corrugation impact/fatigue.
critic_independent_verification.scope: Specific metro installation only; draft correctly limits transfer to plausibility of bracket dynamics.

sources.title: Siemens Mobility takes part in Network Rail trials to predict rough rides
sources.released_version_or_commit: Siemens Mobility press release dated 2022-04-22; trial status reported one month into a six-month operational trial.
sources.locator: Lines 16–34, especially trial fleet, predecessor simulation, progress and product architecture.
sources.observed_operation: Siemens reported its TBCM application in a Network Rail Lot 1 trial on 80 South Western Railway trains in the Wessex region; five other manufacturers' systems were also in the trial. The product used the existing GSM-R cab-radio platform; press release says it was one month into operation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Vendor report, early in a six-month trial; states an initial rough-ride prediction result but supplies no independent metrics or post-trial evaluation in this page.
sources.applicability: Shows a comparator's route from simulation to multi-train operational trial and dependence on rail data/GSM-R; its claims, sensors, location performance and thresholds do not transfer to a cart.

critic_independent_verification.access: Official Siemens release opened and checked.
critic_independent_verification.locator_checked: Lines 17–27: 80 SWR trains, Wessex, GSM-R platform and one month into a six-month multi-vendor trial; page is vendor-authored.
critic_independent_verification.scope: Early vendor-reported implementation history; it supplies no independent performance metrics.

note: Source claims are bounded by the listed locators and conditions; applicability is stated per source. No live or physical measurements were taken.

reviser_critique_dispositions.decision: reject unsupported-finding conclusion; amend for precision
reviser_critique_dispositions.rationale: Publisher full-text result explicitly reports Run 36 capturing the same known fault as Run 25; retain rail-specific context and transfer limitations.
Fixed-reference null is non-diagnostic outside its coverage; add coverage/acquisition checks and qualified-engineering review for a persistent mapped event.
A reference channel corroborates local response; qualified inspection is needed for defect attribution and safety judgment.

Replication and stopping criteria depend on the unresolved endpoint and baseline variation; define precision target, minimum/maximum passes, interim points, and inconclusive result rule before testing.
Two combined load configurations do not isolate mass from placement; vary separately only in a justified follow-on design.
